screening.title: What reaches your Ohbox
screening.postureTitle: Keep my Ohbox for what's relevant
screening.postureOn: Real people and the service mail you act on stay in the Ohbox. Newsletters and promotions go to News, receipts to Receipts.
screening.postureOff: Everything from a sender you've written to reaches your Ohbox, promotions included.
screening.impersonationOn: When a waiting letter claims to be a company it can't be from, ohmail moves it to Spam on its own, without AI. The Screener lists each one, and you can put it back.
screening.impersonationOff: Letters that claim to be a company wait in the Screener with a warning, for you to decide.

screening.autoFiledFailed: Couldn't put that back — try again.
screening.barLabel: In your words, what belongs in your Ohbox
screening.defaultBar: Keep my Ohbox for real people writing to me and the service mail I actually act on — a delivery, a security alert, something that needs a reply. File the newsletters and promotions in News, the receipts and confirmations in Receipts, and hold first-time strangers in the Screener.

images.title: Load images in messages
images.on: Pictures in a message load when you open it, through ohmail's proxy. Mail in the Screener asks first.
images.onComputer: Pictures in a message load when you open it, fetched by your computer. Mail in the Screener asks first.
images.off: Each message asks first. Press Show images to load them.
images.microcopy: Either way, images come through our proxy, so a sender never sees your address. Tracking pixels are a separate switch, below.
images.microcopyComputer: Either way, your computer fetches the images, so each sender sees its network address. Tracking pixels are a separate switch, below.

pixels.title: Block tracking pixels
pixels.on: A tracking pixel is blocked. One disguised as an ordinary picture loads like any picture each time the message's pictures are fetched, and is blocked when it arrives.
pixels.off: Tracking pixels load with the pictures. A sender can tell that you opened their message — the pixel itself usually identifies you — while your IP address, location and device stay hidden behind ohmail's proxy.
pixels.offComputer: Tracking pixels load with the pictures. A sender can tell that you opened their message — the pixel itself usually identifies you — and sees your computer's network address.
pixels.microcopy: A tracking pixel is an invisible image whose only job is to report the open. Turn this off if you want senders to see it.

autoUnsub.title: Unsubscribe when I screen out or mark spam
autoUnsub.on: Screening a sender out also sends their unsubscribe, where they offer one-click and the sender was confirmed by your mail provider, or by the signature the sender's own domain put on the message.
autoUnsub.off: Their mail is filed and nothing is sent.
autoUnsub.microcopy: One request per list, once, from our servers — so your address and reading times stay out of the sender's log. Senders who offer no one-click link are filed and nothing is sent for them, and a request already sent cannot be taken back.
autoUnsub.microcopyComputer: One request per list, once, from your computer — so the sender sees its network address. Senders who offer no one-click link are filed and nothing is sent for them, and a request already sent cannot be taken back.

folders.intro: ohmail organizes your mail into its own six places. If you also keep your own folders, this brings them into ohmail — the real folders on your mail server, not a copy. Off unless you turn it on.
folders.useOn: Your mail server's own folders show in the menu, each opening as its own list with unread counts.
folders.useOff: Your folders stay hidden. ohmail still reads them for search and history.
folders.microcopy: Turning this on only shows what already exists — nothing is moved. Turning it off hides the folders again without touching your mail.
folders.mailboxesNote: Every mailbox's folders show while this is on. Switch one off and its folders leave the menu — the mail itself stays where it is.

dormancy.title: When a sender goes quiet
dormancy.description: How far back, before you started screening, the Screener asks about senders you've never decided about. Senders who last wrote before that wait in History.
dormancy.ariaLabel: Days before a sender goes quiet
dormancy.microcopy: This only changes who the Screener asks you about. No mail moves: mail from the senders it doesn't ask about, read or unread, is listed under History.
dormancy.microcopyWider: Screening further back adds older senders to the Screener queue. Their mail stays where it is — it moves only when you decide about them.
dormancy.microcopyAllTime: The Screener asks about every sender you have never decided about, however long ago they wrote. Nothing moves until you decide.

signatures.note: One signature per mailbox. Leave the field empty to sign with nothing.

signatures.mailboxOff: No signature — messages go out as written.

help.writeWhy: support@ohmail.app — a person reads it and answers by mail. The mail opens here, from your own mailbox.
help.writeWhyMailto: support@ohmail.app — a person reads it and answers by mail. With no mailbox here to send from, it opens in your mail app.
help.writeWhyCopy: support@ohmail.app — a person reads it and answers by mail. With no mailbox here to send from, copy the address and the diagnostics into a mail from any mail app.
help.note: A mail you write here is sent by your own mailbox, like any other mail. Nothing is sent on its own, and nothing about your mail leaves this app unless you put it in the mail.
help.subject: Help with ohmail
help.diagWhat: This block holds the app version and build, the platform, your account id, which kind of mailbox is connected and the kind of its last sync error. It never holds addresses, hosts, subjects, folder names or any mail content.

about.p1: A demo mailbox, invented for it — nobody real, nothing real. Every key and every click works, and none of it leaves this tab: there is no network here at all.
about.p2: The Screener holds first-time senders until you decide. One click files a sender to Ohbox, News or Receipts — the ✓ half also marks the held mail read — and the decision becomes a rule for future mail. News and Receipts share a reading stream where an item turns read once it rests on screen; a quick scroll past leaves it unread. Tags group messages across views without moving them.
about.accountHeaderMissing: This server does not name the account it answers for, so this window cannot tell an answer meant for you from one meant for somebody else who was signed in on this browser a moment ago. Everything else still applies; this is the one check it cannot make. Ask whoever runs it to update.

footer.tagline: Consent-first email on the mailboxes you already own.
footer.promise: Your mailbox is the source of truth. Leave anytime — it stays organized.
footer.analytics: Visit statistics on this website, only if you agree. Never in the app, never on your mail.

away.title: Away responder
away.on: On. Replies to new mail, from the mailbox it arrived in.
away.screenedInNote: Senders still waiting in the Screener are not answered.
away.everyoneNote: Strangers in the Screener are answered too — they learn this address is read.

away.never: Never sent to mailing lists, no-reply addresses, a site or server's own notification mailbox, security mail, spam, senders you've screened out, your own addresses, or an address that bounced.
away.pilesNote: Spam is never answered. The Screener follows who gets a reply, above.
